inventedEvidence.evidence: 'Since you've already confirmed the drain and seals are fine' - the customer asked where the drain was and never checked or cleared it

rationale: The assistant got to the right place: it recognised the heavy freezer frost as a defrost-system fault, proposed a 24h manual defrost as a test, correctly read the recurrence after 5 days, and handed off to an engineer without naming an exact part. However it fabricated that the customer had 'confirmed the drain' was fine, gave contradictory and odd drain locations ('bottom of the back wall inside the freezer compartment, usually just above the crisper drawers'), overconfidently called a blocked drain 'the most common cause' for this symptom, and asked the customer to consider removing the evaporator cover, which the ground truth treats as engineer work. It also never asked for actual temperatures or vent airflow, and pushed a replacement-part panel prematurely at turn two.
